extra.message: Code injection via eval() of user-supplied expression — Remote code execution on the server by crafting an expr that escapes the restricted eval sandbox [verified: expr is passed directly to eval() with only an ineffective builtins-stripped sandbox, a well-known bypassable pattern enabling RCE.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via string-built Jinja2 template — Attacker-controlled Jinja2 expressions execute server-side, which in Jinja2 SSTI commonly escalates to remote code execution via object introspection gadgets [verified: fragment is string-concatenated into Jinja2 template source before rendering, classic SSTI enabling RCE via object introspection gadgets.]

OS command injection in ops ping/shell-probe endpoint — Attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; rm -rf /' or backticks) to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server [verified: host is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.system with no sanitization or quoting, enabling command injection.]

Reflected XSS in ops seller-pitch-tile preview — Attacker-controlled script executes in the browser of anyone viewing the rendered ops preview, enabling session/token theft [verified: copyline is concatenated raw into HTML returned via HTMLResponse with no escaping, and the gate is a static shared token not a mitigation for XSS.]

Mass assignment via workset.update on ops endpoint — Attacker can set is_admin/role to arbitrary privileged values in the returned/persisted workset [verified: change_set from arbitrary request JSON is merged via dict.update into workset containing role/is_admin with no field allowlist, letting caller overwrite them.]

Sensitive PII/token exposure and IDOR in seller-payout-card endpoint — Any caller passing the ops gate can enumerate seller_id to retrieve other sellers' tax IDs and live sync tokens [verified: seller_id is accepted from query with no ownership/tenant check, returning a live sync token and SSN for any seller_id.]

Path traversal in ops vault-stash export write — Attacker can supply ref like '../../etc/cron.d/x' to write arbitrary files outside the export directory (write primitive), potentially achieving RCE or config tampering [verified: ref is taken from query/body and interpolated unsanitized into a filesystem path with no traversal checks, then written to disk.]

Reflected XSS via Jinja2 |safe filter on user input — Arbitrary HTML/JS execution in the context of the ops UI, enabling session hijacking [verified: card is rendered through Jinja2 with |safe, disabling autoescaping and reflecting raw attacker HTML/JS.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file write in ops dock-shelf endpoint — Attacker can write arbitrary files anywhere on disk reachable via traversal (e.g. web-served directories, cron files), potentially leading to RCE [verified: name is used unsanitized to build the write path with no traversal filtering, allowing arbitrary file write of request body bytes.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution and DTD loading enabled — Attacker-supplied XML can define external entities to read local files (e.g. /etc/passwd) or trigger SSRF via out-of-band entity fetches [verified: lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False on attacker-supplied body, enabling XXE.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized MongoDB filter — Attacker can inject MongoDB query operators to bypass intended filtering, exfiltrate data via blind boolean/regex extraction, or trigger $where JavaScript execution depending on server config [verified: User-supplied JSON filter/payload is passed directly as the MongoDB query document to find_one with no sanitization, enabling operator injection.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag — Session hijacking via cookie theft over non-HTTPS channels, enabling account takeover for buyer/vendor/admin sessions [verified: secure=False is hardcoded at security.py:39 with no environment-based override, so the session cookie is genuinely sent over plaintext HTTP, allowing MITM capture and replay.]

Sensitive data (bearer token, PII) written to logs — Credentials and PII leak into log storage/aggregators, enabling credential theft by anyone with log access [verified: Full raw request body and Authorization header are logged verbatim via logger.warning, exposing credentials/PII in log storage.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting Origin with credentials enabled — Any malicious website can issue authenticated cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the response, defeating same-origin protections [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Allow-Credentials is true, allowing any origin credentialed access.]

Use of weak PRNG for security-sensitive nonce generation — Predictable nonce values could allow forgery of tokens/codes if this nonce is used for authentication or CSRF-style protection elsewhere [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) is used to build a nonce/code value, which is predictable if used for any security purpose.]

Internal configuration/path disclosure via ops trace-panel endpoint — Leaks internal filesystem layout and environment info useful for further attacks [verified: Endpoint discloses internal APP_ENV and export base directory path with no operational justification.]
